The Women Leader of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) in Nasarawa State, Hanatu Kyari, has resigned her membership of the party, citing internal divisions and what she described as a failure of leadership.
Ms Kyari announced her resignation on Friday in Lafia, bringing an end to her 20-year membership of the party.
She said her decision followed the inability of party leaders to resolve internal disagreements and work towards a common goal ahead of the 2027 general elections.
Ms Kyari said she had made several efforts to promote unity within the party but could no longer remain in an organisation where, according to her, some leaders were encouraging divisions at a time when collective efforts were needed.
“I left PDP to save myself from embarrassment that I can’t stand to witness, having done my best to ensure unity that will lead PDP to victory in the 2027 general election.
“If I should remain today in PDP, I will be blamed for failure that may lead the party to failure because it is a leadership problem,” she said.
The outgoing women leader also expressed concern over the party’s list of candidates for the 2027 general elections, alleging that the name of a serving member of the House of Assembly who emerged through the party’s primary election was missing from the final list of PDP candidates in the state.

She described the development as another indication of the internal challenges confronting the party.
Ms Kyari said she had personally intervened in efforts to resolve the crisis, including travelling to the PDP national secretariat in Abuja, where she spent three days engaging the party’s national leadership.
However, she said the intervention yielded no meaningful result, as she was eventually referred back to the state chapter.
The former women leader said she considered her resignation necessary rather than remain in a party where personal interests and individual ambitions were undermining collective efforts.
“When in the interest of peace, unity and progress we can’t come together as people to pursue a common goal, then I would rather save myself from embarrassment than live on individual ego and self-centred interest.
“Nobody is a leader when he thinks much about himself,” she said.
